deliverables.README.md: assessment + two design options (A fixed caps, B dynamic capacity+dispatch) + minimal mitigation C + impact and decisions
deliverables.facts.json: machine-readable facts: current caps, guards, scratch, upstream dynamic rules, A1 identity, fixture geometry, S4 record, memory budgets, design costs
deliverables.manifest.txt: sha256/bytes for the three files above (does not register itself)

key_findings: A1 (commit 307219fe) raised FACE_MAX 16->20 and clip buffers 32->40 offline; DEG_MAX stays 10; no GPU window has validated it, so U8 device count=4 is an expectation, not a measurement.

Residual gap after A1 has two dimensions: polygon vertices > 20 (face) and vertex degree > 10 (degree); the degree dimension is untouched by A1 and is triggered by fan/apex/pole vertices in ordinary triangulated meshes.

Upstream capacity is model-driven (max(m.npolygonmax, 16|4) and max(m.nmeshdegmax, 3)) with global per-ccd scratch arrays; device uses fixed per-thread arrays. This is a semantic difference, not an upstream limitation.

Existing M2/M3/S4 fixtures (cube: max face 3, max degree 5) do not trigger either limit; U7/U8 stay record-only. A1 changed the collision kernel identity (source 254,005/9b7435ab -> 254,263/12d50d68, PTX 3,883,769/6 entries), so any later collision window needs a fresh freeze; references need no recapture.
open_decisions: Whether to implement C (host-side explicit diagnostic for over-cap models) and its policy (count/warn/Unsupported).
A tier choice: 24/24 vs 32/32 (recommendation: 32/32), and whether degree is raised in the same change.
Whether U8 is upgraded from record-only to pass/fail (user signature item).
Whether B is backlogged and whether B2b is the path for a general-mesh-coverage commitment.
Any device change requires user approval + a new window plan (new suite, new freeze, U8 assertion method).
